messages:
incident-bot: ALERT P1 — GPU pool 'prod-gpu-a' queue growth >95% (3m). Throttling engaged. Affected: inference and embeddings. Link: https://ops.redwood/in/2478019999

infra-oncall: paging @sre_lead @runtime_eng @ml_serving @ops — huge queue growth, clients seeing 5xx/429s

sre_lead: I see ready->queued spike across two zones. Autoscaler attempted 6 scale operations, all failed with cloud quota/insufficient resources. Also driver errors (Xid) on a subset of nodes.

runtime_eng: grabbing logs from gpu-node-23, 24. Repro shows repeated kernel OOM + CUDA Xid. Snippet:
```
[2026-04-12T12:07:03Z] nvidia: Xid (79) Resetting GPU
[2026-04-12T12:07:04Z] containerd: oom-kill: process=python pid=2345
[2026-04-12T12:07:05Z] kubelet: Evicting pod runc-... reason=OOMKilled
```

ml_serving: nodes are flapping — effective GPU capacity down ~40% in affected pools. Autoscaler log shows quota error: `ERROR: failed to create instance (insufficientQuota) - requested GPUs=8 region=us-west`

ops: confirmed quota checks — we're at regional GPU quota limit for the preferred instance family. Autoscaler has no fallback configured.

infra-oncall: options: 1) cordon+drain flapping nodes, 2) rollback recent driver rollout, 3) request emergency quota bump, 4) switch autoscaler to alternate instance family. Which do we want now?

sre_lead: short-term: cordon gpu-node-23/24, pause low-priority jobs, and start fallback scale with alternate instance type in us-west. Also rollback driver canary; last driver rollout was ~11:50 that introduced new kernel module.

ops: opening cloud ticket now (CS-89234) for quota increase. ETA unknown. Can do fallback family (a100-legacy) with spare quota.

runtime_eng: I can roll driver back to previous build (2026-04-11) which was stable. Will do a canary (10% nodes) first. Rollback command:
```
kubectl -n kube-system set image ds/nvidia-driver driver=image:2026-04-11
```

incident-bot: On-call Handoff scheduled in 30m: infra-oncall -> runtime_eng. Escalation to SRE manager if unresolved in 60m.

customer-success: CS note: Customers on dedicated pools (acct-A, acct-B) reporting elevated errors and latency for embeddings. CS lead Priya notified customers. Preparing external status update.

sre_lead: Also throttle background/async workloads to preserve capacity for realtime routes. Can we flip priority queues?

infra-oncall: toggled priority queueing, paused batch re-encodes and async backfills. Monitoring queue length and throttle metrics.

runtime_eng: canary rollback started on 5 nodes. Observing Xid and OOM counters.

(5m later)

runtime_eng: canary stable for 4m. Xid events fell from ~12/min to ~1/min on canary nodes. Rolling full rollback across ds.

incident-bot: Update: Autoscaler still hitting quota for preferred family; fallback scale to alternate family in-progress (requested 4 instances). Cloud ticket #CS-89234 created.

sre_lead: rollback complete. Uncordoning drained nodes in controlled fashion. Queue length trending down, token latency improving.

infra-oncall: current effective GPU capacity back to ~90% of baseline. Queue draining, request latencies returning to normal. Keeping a 2h elevated watch.

customer-success: External status updated: mitigation in progress; residual 429s expected for 15-30m. Sent communication to affected accounts.

runtime_eng: follow-ups (to-do): [1] Add autoscaler fallback to alternative instance family automatically, [2] add quota preflight check and alert, [3] pin driver releases + automated rollback on Xid surge, [4] postmortem with RCA and timeline.

sre_lead: handing off monitoring to next shift. If any regressions, page SRE manager.

infra-oncall: handing off to next oncall @emma at 2478020899

emma: acknowledged — will maintain watches, hold links to quota ticket and rollback runbook.

(Notes)
- Root causes likely: driver kernel module regression combined with regional GPU quota exhaustion forcing autoscaler into a dead-end.
- Impact: temporary degraded throughput and increased 429/5xx for some hosted and dedicated customers.
- Short-term mitigation: rollback driver, fallback instance family scale, throttle background jobs.
- Long-term actions captured above.
